comparison: Perfect agreement on HG gyrification patterns (C6-C9). Both evaluations support the descriptive statistics and characterization of HG patterns. Peer reviewers noted this examination as 'rare and therefore valuable,' while OpenEval confirmed internal consistency and lack of demographic confounds.

Perfect agreement on within-hemisphere functional-structural relationships (C31-C38). Both support the complex hemisphere-specific patterns. Peer reviewers emphasized microstructural asymmetries as especially important, while OpenEval noted modest effect sizes (R=0.11-0.20) but appropriate statistical testing.

Perfect agreement on specificity controls (C39-C41). Both evaluations support these findings as demonstrating PT-specific relationships rather than general brain-behavior correlations. Peer reviewers accepted this as strengthening the main structure-function claims.

Strong agreement on methodological reliability (C3-C5, C80-C81). Both evaluations praised the inter-rater reliability and methodological rigor. Peer reviewers highlighted 'large sample size, inter-rater reliability, and corrections for multiple comparisons' as strengths. OpenEval noted the lower bound ICC (0.55) suggests moderate rather than excellent reproducibility for some measures.

Strong agreement on macrostructural findings (C17-C21). Both support the differential effects of HG gyrification on PT structural measures. Peer reviewers suggested authors could 'emphasise on their interesting macrostructural results' more, indicating acceptance with encouragement for greater prominence. OpenEval noted complexity of patterns is well-documented but biological interpretation not fully developed.

Strong agreement on HG duplication effects on PT functional lateralization (C13-C15). Both evaluations support this as a key finding. Peer reviewers emphasized this as central to 'the structure-function relationship of planum temporale asymmetry in lateralised language processing.' OpenEval noted moderate effect sizes and internal consistency but unexplained mechanism.

Strong agreement on functional-structural coupling at asymmetry level (C25-C30). Both support these findings as core contributions. Peer reviewers highlighted 'especially microstructural asymmetries are related to functional auditory language asymmetries' as the main finding. OpenEval noted modest but highly significant effect sizes (R=0.11-0.26) with appropriate statistical correction.

Partial agreement on main conclusions (C58-C59, C71). Both support the overall findings. Peer reviewers emphasized the work's contribution to 'an ongoing and long-standing debate about structural and functional brain asymmetries.' OpenEval raised concerns about modest effect sizes limiting causal interpretation and potential overstatement of 'first empirical evidence' claim.

Agreement on microstructural-functional relationship conclusion (C72). Both evaluations support this main conclusion. Peer reviewers explicitly emphasized this as serving 'as a reference for future targeted-studies on brain lateralization.' OpenEval supported the claim but noted correlational nature and modest effect sizes limit causal interpretation.

Agreement on behavioral correlation findings (C23). Both evaluations accepted the weak vocabulary correlation. OpenEval rated as UNCERTAIN due to apparent contradiction with C12 and very small effect size (R=0.10, p=0.047) raising Type I error concerns. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted without critique.

Agreement on HG morphology effects (C16). Both evaluations support findings on how HG gyrification affects PT properties. Peer reviewers suggested greater emphasis on macrostructural results. OpenEval supported the pattern but noted unexplained mechanism linking HG to PT function.

Agreement on independence of structure-function coupling from HG pattern (C70). Both evaluations support this finding. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted through overall positive assessment. OpenEval confirmed internal consistency and independence of asymmetry-level and within-hemisphere analyses.

Agreement on robustness of functional-structural coupling (C69). Both evaluations support this aspect of the findings. Peer reviewers accepted as part of key structure-function relationship. OpenEval confirmed findings support independence of different analytical approaches.

Agreement on functional-structural coupling findings (C24). Both evaluations support the significant coupling at asymmetry level. Peer reviewers accepted as part of comprehensive HG gyrification analysis. OpenEval noted appropriate statistical correction and modest but significant effect sizes.

Partial overlap on participant characteristics (C2). OpenEval evaluated broader participant selection criteria (C1-C2, C73-C74) as supported. Peer reviewers praised 'large sample size' as a methodological strength but did not specifically evaluate participant selection claims.

Minimal overlap on structural measures (C22). OpenEval evaluated comprehensive structural effects (C17-C22) as supported despite complex patterns. Peer reviewers acknowledged HG morphology effects on PT properties with suggestion for greater emphasis.

OpenEval evaluated bilateral PT involvement and functional factors (C10-C11) as supported, noting factor interpretation as somewhat inferential. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims about task design and factor analysis.

OpenEval evaluated literature review claims (C42-C50) as supported, noting accurate characterization of prior work with slight potential overstatement of consistency of null findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these background literature claims.

OpenEval evaluated biological interpretation of MRI measures (C51-C52, C82-C83) as supported but noted these are indirect proxies without explicit acknowledgment of limitations. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these methodological interpretation claims.

OpenEval evaluated developmental and comparative context claims (C53-C56) as supported, noting appropriate citations but cautioning about causal interpretation. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these contextual claims.

OpenEval rated mechanistic explanations (C60-C62) as UNCERTAIN, noting they are explicitly speculative and go beyond correlational data without direct evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these speculative mechanism claims.

OpenEval evaluated literature on hemispheric specialization (C63-C66) as supported, noting accurate citations providing relevant context. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these background literature claims.

OpenEval evaluated data acquisition and preprocessing procedures (C75-C79, C84) as supported, noting standardized HCP protocols ensure quality but language task not specifically designed for PT research. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these methodological procedure claims.
